summary: The proposal presents a relevant access-management problem and a concrete platform and evaluation direction. However, the abstract requires expansion, the Problem section mixes in workaround descriptions, and pervasive first-person narration and smaller wording inconsistencies require revision before submission.

findings.title: Abstract is too short
findings.description: The abstract is substantially shorter than the required 1/3–1/2 page. Expand it with a concise statement of the research problem, the specific contribution, and the evaluation approach until it meets the minimum length.

locations.quote: **A university research chair grants access to its compute hosts, chat workspace, and code repositories by hand, while the people who need that access change every semester.**

findings.title: Problem section includes workaround alternatives
findings.description: The Problem section presents alternative approaches or workarounds, despite the requirement that it describe only problems and their negative consequences. Remove these solution descriptions from the Problem section; describe only the underlying access-management failure and its impact, or move discussion of alternatives to a separate design-related section.

locations.quote: A student who needs a host, a channel, and a repository asks several people and waits for each of them, and some **bridge the delay with a shared login** that hides who acted.

The common workaround **hands maintainers full administrative rights**, which violates the principle of least privilege [SS75] and exposes every user and every host to a mistake made for a single project.

findings.title: Excessive first-person narration
findings.description: The proposal repeatedly uses first-person narration despite the guideline to avoid “I.” Replace it with an explicit subject such as “the thesis,” “the platform,” or “the implementation,” using first person only when necessary to describe the research approach.

locations.quote: In this thesis, **I develop** a self-service platform on which every grant carries an expiry date from the moment somebody requests it.
In this thesis, **I develop** a self-service platform on which requesters ask for time-limited access, maintainers decide, and access ends on its own.

locations.section: 4.1 Unify Heterogeneous Resources in One Tree
locations.quote: **I implement** the keycloak-group, slack-channel, github-team, and webhook connectors, whose credentials administrators configure at runtime.

locations.section: 4.2 Enforce an Expiry Date on Every Grant
locations.quote: **I evaluate** correctness with an automated scenario that provisions SSH, Slack, and GitHub access from one approval.

locations.section: 4.3 Delegate the Approval of Requests to Maintainers
locations.quote: **I reach** this objective when administrators perform fewer manual actions and requesters wait less than in the current process.
**I divide** the work into six iterations of four weeks, each ending with a vertically integrated increment that a user can try in the web application.

locations.section: Transparency in the Use of AI Tools
locations.quote: **I used** Claude Code to draft the text of the abstract and of Sections 1 to 5, to author the three diagrams in Typst, and to search for the cited publications.

findings.title: Passive constructions obscure actors
findings.description: Several clauses use passive voice or reduced passive constructions without identifying the actor. Rewrite them with explicit subjects, particularly where the responsible system or person matters for the proposal’s design.

locations.quote: Requests travel by chat message or e-mail, nobody records an end date, and **access granted for one project** outlives the time a person spends at the chair.

locations.section: 4.1 Unify Heterogeneous Resources in One Tree
locations.quote: I model the resources as a tree whose folders pass maintainership, audit policy, and grants down to **leaves bound to target systems**.

locations.section: 4.2 Enforce an Expiry Date on Every Grant
locations.quote: I evaluate correctness with an automated scenario that provisions SSH, Slack, and GitHub access from one approval, and, in a second run with **the workflow engine disabled on purpose**, the drift check reports the remaining SSH membership.

findings.title: Inconsistent term for the approval role
findings.description: Use one term consistently for the approval role. The prose introduces “supervisors” as an apparent synonym for “maintainers,” while the rest of the proposal uses “maintainers.” Replace “supervisors” with “maintainers,” or explicitly define a distinction if these are separate roles.

locations.quote: **Maintainers, the supervisors who know whether a request is legitimate,** cannot act on it, while the administrators who can act lack the context to judge it and become a bottleneck.
